title: [D2 Context] View-layering boundary tests and materialization policy
summary: Every object the migrations create now declares itself above its CREATE -- Layer / Object / Reads / Read by -- and helena.migrations.declarations() refuses a file that does not, refuses a Reads: that is prose, refuses an Object: that disagrees with the CREATE under it, and refuses a MATERIALIZED VIEW whose Read by: names nobody. tests/test_view_layering.py (21 tests) turns the flatten -> signal -> analytical rule into something that fails: it asserts every Reads: line equal to rw_catalog.rw_depend on a running engine before drawing any conclusion from a comment, then applies helena.migrations.MAY_READ over those verified edges. scripts/dev_check.py --storage (make storage) reports what each relation of a migrated schema stores, so the materialization cost is read off the engine instead of argued.
assumption_validated: Four measurements, all against RisingWave 3.0.3 and all now tests. (1) THE ENGINE RECORDS DEPENDENCIES THROUGH PLAIN VIEWS: rw_depend holds the transitive closure expanded through plain views and stopping at tables and materialized views, because a plain view is inlined into the plan of whatever reads it. That is checkable both ways -- the closure computed from the 30 declaration blocks equals rw_depend exactly -- so a declaration comment can be validated by execution rather than believed, which is what makes a comment-based layering rule honest. It is also the mechanism the materialization policy rests on: a plain view is not a cheap object, it is not an object. (2) A PLAIN VIEW STORES NOTHING, measured: with records in the store and the whole signal layer running, all 19 plain views report 0 bytes in rw_table_stats and every byte reported belongs to a table or a materialized view. (3) MATERIALIZING AN INTERMEDIATE THAT ONLY FEEDS AN AGGREGATE COSTS, measured twice on the same two pipelines producing the same aggregate: +12 % over the ten-record layer capture (142 064 -> 159 194 bytes) and +56 % over 73 flow rows collapsing into 2 contexts (119 154 -> 186 236 bytes). (4) NEGATIVE RESULT, recorded rather than smoothed over: concept/03-architecture.md's 42 % IS NOT REPRODUCED and is not reproducible as a rate -- the penalty is the aggregation factor, not a constant. The note's figure is one workload's number; the direction is what holds, and the direction is what the test asserts.
makes_buildable: The first analytical view (D3, the enriched context) is now built against a rule that can fail rather than against a sentence in a note: it declares Layer: analytical, and reading helena_flatten_% or helena_normalized_events -- directly or by a stale comment -- fails tests/test_view_layering.py. helena.migrations.declarations() is also a parsed inventory of the schema (30 objects, kind, layer, edges, readers) that any later increment can query instead of grepping SQL. And every increment that adds an object now has an enforced habit: declare it, name its readers, and name it in the Read by: of everything it reads.

verification.detail: 593 passed in 156.9 s, full suite, against a throwaway in-memory ./bin/risingwave single_node (21 of them new). Every SQL claim is executed: the declared kinds are read back out of information_schema, the declared reads are compared to rw_catalog.rw_depend, and the storage numbers come from rw_catalog.rw_table_stats with records in the store. `uv lock --check` and `python -m compileall src tests scripts` are clean. Mutation-checked three ways, each restored byte-identically (md5 verified) and re-run green: changing 0006's `Reads: helena_flatten_flows` to `helena_normalized_events` fails three tests (the layering rule, the engine comparison and Read-by completeness); dropping helena_signal_host_context from helena_flatten_flows's `Read by:` fails test_every_relation_that_reads_an_object_is_named_in_its_read_by; deleting the `Layer:` field from 0002 turns 7 tests red. The 42 %-probe test's own numbers were reproduced identically across two runs.

invariant_conflicts.step: Write a test that parses the migration SQL and asserts no analytical view references the flatten layer or a source directly
invariant_conflicts.conflict: prds/CONTEXT.md is explicit that a test asserting on SQL text is not a test -- it finds the comment arguing for a thing's absence -- and instruction.md §7 requires SQL to be exercised by execution. A parser over the .sql files alone would have been exactly the forbidden shape, and worse here than usual, because the thing parsed IS a comment.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Both, in order. The declaration comments are parsed from the files (they are the only place a layer label can live -- the engine strips comments), and then test_the_declared_reads_are_the_dependencies_the_engine_recorded proves the parsed `Reads:` edges equal rw_catalog.rw_depend on a running engine, expanded through plain views. The layering rule is then applied to edges the engine has agreed with. A comment that drifted from its SQL fails at the engine comparison before it can make the layering test agree with a lie.

invariant_conflicts.step: Document the measured cost -- a materialized intermediate feeding only an aggregate cost 42% more disk
invariant_conflicts.conflict: instruction.md §5 forbids claiming more than was demonstrated and forbids generalizing a measurement. Repeating '42 %' as this repository's number would have been repeating someone else's measurement as ours; measuring it here and reporting the result as '42 %' would have been worse.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Measured here, twice, and reported as what it is: +12 % and +56 % on two inputs, with the reason they differ (the aggregation factor) stated. concept/03-architecture.md's 42 % is cited as a third workload's number that this repository does not reproduce, and the note is NOT edited -- it records a real measurement from elsewhere, and correcting it would need the workload it was taken on. What the test asserts is the direction.

deferred: An analytical object. There is none yet, so the row of MAY_READ the invariant is actually about is exercised on a synthetic migration file rather than on this repository's SQL. The rule fires; nothing here has had the chance to break it.

Enforcing that `Read by:` names ALL readers rather than all relation readers. Every relation that declares `Reads: X` must appear in X's `Read by:` and that is asserted; a module or a test named there is only checked for existing on disk. Requiring a Python reader to be provable would mean parsing call sites, which is a static-analysis project and not this one.
A rule about which SQL a view may contain. The declarations say what an object reads, not how. Nothing above needs more yet.

Making the flatten layer's plainness a rule rather than a list. tests/test_context.py::test_every_flatten_object_is_a_plain_view already asserts every helena_flatten_% object is a VIEW, by prefix; that is the check, and duplicating it as a policy rule here would be two answers to one question.

Dropping the leaked `probe_retained` materialized view in tests/test_context.py (see lessons). Fixing another task's test is outside this task; the new tests are scoped to the `helena_` prefix so they are correct either way.
lessons: task 17: rw_catalog.rw_depend records dependencies EXPANDED THROUGH PLAIN VIEWS and stopping at tables and materialized views -- a plain view is inlined into the plan of whatever reads it, so an MV over a view over a table depends on all three. Measured: the closure computed from the declaration blocks equals rw_depend exactly over all 30 objects. This is why a plain view costs nothing, and it is what makes `Reads:` comments checkable against a running engine.

task 17: Per-relation storage is available from rw_catalog.rw_table_stats (id, total_key_count, total_key_size, total_value_size) joined to rw_catalog.rw_internal_tables on job_id -- the object's own rows plus the streaming state behind it, which is where most of a materialized view's disk goes. It is the engine's own accounting, an estimate that moves as compaction runs (the same schema reported 3.07 MB and 4.35 MB minutes apart), so use it for shape and direction, not as a du.

task 17: A plain view reports EXACTLY zero bytes there, with data loaded and the layer above running. The materialization policy is therefore observable in one query rather than arguable: `make storage` / `uv run scripts/dev_check.py --storage`.

task 17: The 42 % in concept/03-architecture.md is not a rate. Measured on two inputs here: +12 % (10 records) and +56 % (73 flow rows, 2 contexts). The penalty is the aggregation factor, so the note's number should be read as evidence the cost is real, never as a coefficient.

task 17: EDITING AN APPLIED MIGRATION -- even comments only -- changes its sha256 and the runner refuses the store: '0001_schema_migrations.sql has changed since it was applied'. Verified by running scripts/migrate.py against an engine migrated before the retrofit. Nothing is deployed so this cost nothing now; from here on a declaration goes in the file that creates the object.

task 17: The migrated schema is SHARED for the whole run and tests build `probe_` objects in it. tests/test_context.py's eviction test leaves `probe_retained` behind, so anything asserting on the schema's whole contents must scope itself (the new tests use the `helena_` prefix). Worth knowing before writing another catalogue-wide assertion.

task 17: The full suite is now 593 tests in ~157 s on this machine, not the ~2 143 s task 16 recorded. Same fixtures; the difference is a warm machine. Do not budget a session around the larger number.
failed_approaches: task 17: Deriving the layering edges from rw_depend alone. It cannot work: rw_depend expands through plain views, so helena_signal_context_entities legitimately 'depends on' helena_normalized_events and every signal object would read as a source-reading violation. The direct edges have to come from the declarations, and rw_depend is what validates them -- which is why the closure function exists.

task 17: Matching `Object:` by searching the field for 'VIEW'. It read helena_normalized_events -- 'TABLE. The record as read, held so that every view above is a view over one stored copy' -- as a VIEW. The match is anchored at the start of the field now, optionally after 'plain'.

task 17: Asserting in the probe test that the materialized intermediate alone stores more than the whole plain-view pipeline. True at 73 flow rows (131 594 vs 119 154), false at 10 (103 146 vs 142 064). Only the total and the direction are asserted; the size is the aggregation factor.

task 17: `git checkout <file>` to undo a mutation-test edit. It reverts to HEAD, which discarded every uncommitted edit to that file, not just the mutation -- the 0005 Read-by retrofit had to be reapplied. Copy the file aside and copy it back, and verify with md5sum, which is what the other mutations did.

task 17: Testing the --storage refusal by pointing report_storage at a DSN with a bogus search_path. Fragile against an engine someone had already migrated into `public`. The formatting and the refusal are now `storage_report(mapping)`, tested against a real empty schema from the engine_schema fixture.
next_session_should_know: The layering rule is now enforced and the enforcement is in helena.migrations, not in the tests: declarations() parses the four-field block above every CREATE, layering_violations() applies MAY_READ, reads_the_engine_records() expands the declared edges the way the engine does. tests/test_view_layering.py is where all of it fails. Four things to know before adding an object. (1) YOUR CREATE NEEDS A DECLARATION BLOCK immediately above it, no blank line, with Layer / Object / Reads / Read by. `Reads:` must be a comma-separated list of relation names or the word `nothing` (a note may follow the first sentence); `Read by:` is prose, and a relation is recognised in it by the helena_ prefix. A materialized view whose Read by: names nobody is refused. (2) YOU MUST ALSO EDIT THE FILES YOU READ FROM: every relation you declare in `Reads:` has to name you in its own `Read by:`, or test_every_relation_that_reads_an_object_is_named_in_its_read_by fails. That is deliberate friction and it is how the old files stopped being stale -- five of them were. (3) The layers are operational / source / reference / flatten / signal / analytical, and the first analytical object may read signal and reference only. Adding a layer means adding a row to MAY_READ, which a test asserts. (4) DO NOT EDIT AN APPLIED MIGRATION, including its comments -- the checksum refusal is real and was measured this session; the retrofit of 0001-0004 and 0008 was the last free one, and any store migrated before it has to be dropped and re-migrated. For the cost side: `make storage` prints what each relation stores, a plain view never appears with a number, and docs/decisions/0016-view-layering-and-materialization-policy.md carries the measurements and says plainly that the concept note's 42 % is not a rate this repository reproduces.
